line: Always grant a role the least permissions that let it work.
Never put an access key in code or in a variable file.
Never open a security group to 0.0.0.0/0 except for a public load balancer.
Always encrypt storage at rest and turn on versioning for buckets that hold state.
Always comment every function, public or private, in at most 2 lines.
Always comment a type, constant, variable or field in at most 1 line.
Always say what the code does; never restate the name.
Never open a comment with a label such as WHY.
Never name a plan, task, ticket, phase or version in a comment.
Never remove or rewrite a comment you did not write.
Always wrap an error with %w and a message that describes the failure.
Never start an error string with the name of the function.
Never discard an error with the blank identifier outside a deferred cleanup.
Never name a package util, common or helpers.
Always declare a sentinel error once at package level, named ErrSomething.
Always write the failing test before the fix.
Always keep tests beside their source and run them with the race detector.
Never use the not-null assertion operator in production code.
Always prefer val and immutable collections over var and mutable ones.
Always run a coroutine in a scope that has an owner.
Never block a thread inside a suspending function.
Always size touch targets to at least 44 by 44 points.
Never hard-code a screen size.
Always give every control a text label for screen readers.
Never carry meaning in color alone.
Always release listeners and observers when the screen goes away.
Never do network or disk work on the main thread.
